status: Research deliverables ready for parent/independent review; public archive and Havenline implementation not performed by this agent.
reading_boundary: All visual observations come from actual decoded source-video frames across the full clip timeline. They are frame-sampling reviews, not claims of continuous video/audio playback. Official documentary descriptions are labeled separately. Existing Havenline footage was reviewed by the other audit agent.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Use visibly directed connections. Each belt has one readable flow direction; each machine socket declares IN or OUT and accepted item type. Rotation must preserve arrow-to-port agreement.
decisions_for_parent.why: Players can predict where an item lands before connecting a belt.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Treat storage receiving and dispatch as different functions with different visible adapters. Receiving adds to bounded inventory. Dispatch releases the requested resource toward a specified machine or counter.
decisions_for_parent.why: A central building otherwise becomes a magical all-to-all pipe that cannot be understood from the camp view.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Keep direct machine-to-next-machine links for recipe intermediates; reserve a branch to storage for buffering and later requests. Do not require every intermediate to make an unnecessary round trip through the house.
decisions_for_parent.why: Short connected chains are easier to read and fit a compact camp. This is a Havenline design inference, not an observed rule of the external games.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Give split, merge and filtered dispatch different functions and silhouettes. A splitter sends one stream to two destinations; a merger meters two arrivals into one free output position; a filter admits compatible items only.
decisions_for_parent.why: A generic decorative intersection hides recipe and bottleneck behavior.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Use explicit full-output behavior: downstream full -> local output buffer holds -> machine waits -> upstream line backs up. No deletion, overlap or conversion of blocked items.
decisions_for_parent.why: Storage capacity and counter demand remain meaningful. Backpressure is documented externally; not measured in Havenline.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Bring finished sale stock into the rear or side of the customer counter. Keep service face, queue and cash collection readable and separately accessible.
decisions_for_parent.why: The other agent directly inspected the user reference showing food feeder lines into an assembler and a service/cash loop. NEW-V08 is metadata-only and must not be cited as visual proof for this.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Protect both bidirectional gate routes and the furnace access area. Use a deliberate bridge, below-grade duct or gate-controlled crossing only where necessary.
decisions_for_parent.why: A belt network must not divide the camp into unreachable islands. Manufacturer lift-gate evidence is an analogy, not a required industrial gate design.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Render the transfer itself: matched elevation, small bridging plate/roller at the handoff, containment on bends and a visible start/end bracket.
decisions_for_parent.why: Different item shapes cannot convincingly travel through empty gaps or sharp decorative corners.

decisions_for_parent.proposal: Use a selected-line flow overlay that identifies destination and the blocked reason, with resource icon and capacity state. Keep the camp view uncluttered otherwise.
decisions_for_parent.why: The exact fault should be understandable without a permanent field of labels.

asset_requests: machine input/output collars with clear arrows
counter rear-stock intake and holding tray
pedestrian crossing in its open and carrying states
acceptance_checks_for_parent: Trace one approved resource from gathering through processing into storage without any missing transfer.
Trace one intermediate from one machine directly to the next relevant machine.
Trace a finished good from storage dispatch to counter rear intake and customer handoff.
Show both gate routes still traversable in both directions and preserve furnace access.
Show full storage and full counter stopping dispatch without lost or overlapping goods.
Show wrong item type rejected or retained safely at a labeled intake.
Confirm every visible arrow agrees with its connection, including bends and camera-facing reversals.
If a bridge/tunnel/gate crosses a walkway, show both traffic routes and appropriate clearance/open state.
